Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO - p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider)

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps so we can run an apples-to-apples qualification. Great to meet you both.

Recap:
- Finlytics priority: end-to-end inference SLOs for production traffic (includes network + model + app glue).
- Targets you mentioned on the call (initial): p95 ~ <= 300 ms, p99 ~ <= 700 ms. Streaming first-byte latency important for the UX.
- Current provider: ModelServeCo (you mentioned) — you see occasional p99 spikes above 1s during concurrent bursts.

Action items / next steps (what we need to qualify):
1) You to send: representative sample payloads (JSONL), a small set of recent traces or client-side telemetry, and an example of your concurrency pattern (burst vs steady qps). Attachment: redwood_perf_data_req.xlsx is the checklist for telemetry/format.
2) Redwood: run a set of baseline tests against our hosted API using your payloads and matching concurrency envelope (we'll test streaming vs non-streaming paths).
3) Tech deep-dive: propose Thu Jul 30 10:00 AM PT for a technical session (latency waterfall, tracing, and test validation).
4) Measurement plan: we'll report p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latencies, first-byte (TTFB) for streaming, throughput at target concurrency, and any behavior under simulated bursts.

Notes / constraints:
- Please provide expected throughput numbers (req/s) and peak concurrency.
- If there are strict regional requirements or VPC-only egress, call out now so we can adjust test routing.

I'll loop in Aditya to lead the baseline tests. We aim to have an initial results summary within 48 hours after we receive samples.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_perf_data_req.xlsx (checklist)

Subject: Re: Performance SLO - p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted API vs current provider)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. Confirming a few data points from our side and attaching the traces you asked for.

Current provider baseline (ModelServeCo):
- Typical steady traffic: 100 req/s, usual concurrency ~100.
- Observed p95: ~420 ms end-to-end; p99: ~1.2 s (spikes under burst).
- Streaming: currently disabled for most endpoints; when enabled, first-byte tends to be ~180 ms.

Streaming requirement for our product: first-token <= 120 ms ideally for best UX; but we can qualify based on your measurements.

Attached: current_provider_traces.zip (server+client traces - redacted), and we'll push the JSONL sample payloads in a follow-up.

We can do Thu Jul 30 10am PT for the deep-dive — Raj and I will join.

—Sara

Thanks Sara — that's very helpful. A few clarifications before we start tests: 

1) Measurement definition: we'll measure end-to-end at the client-side (the same way Finlytics collects it) so numbers are comparable. We'll report p50/p95/p99 plus the streaming first-byte times.
2) Test matrix (what we'll run):
   - Concurrency: 1, 10, 50, 100 (and a burst run to 300 for short bursts).
   - Modes: streaming enabled (server-sent tokens) vs non-streaming.
   - Payload sizes: small/median/large (use the samples you provide).
3) Timeline: once we receive samples and traces we will: provision tests, run baseline (24 hours), run extended burst tests, and deliver a short summary + waterfall traces. Expecting ~48 hours turnaround after samples are received.

Aditya — can you take point on spinning up the runner against our hosted API and match the client-side instrumentation? Please ensure we capture first-byte and total completion times in the same units Finlytics uses.

Sara/Raj — please send sample tokens and the JSONL file requested in the attachment. Also flag any IP allowlist or VPC egress notes.

Thanks,
Marissa
